case_name: Bhaiyan and Another v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

14 October 1977
Cr.A. No. 243 of 1972.
The Judgment was delivered by: JASWANT SINGH, J.
1.  Bhaiyan and Dibia alias Devideen who were tried along with three
facts: The case involves Bhaiyan and Another v State of Madhya Pradesh
Bhaiyan and Dibia alias Devideen were tried along with three others by the Additional Sessions Judge, Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh
The prosecution case is that bad blood existed between the deceased and the appellants
The deceased was a staunch supporter of Congress Party and the appellants were supporters of Jan Sangh Party
There was a re-election of the Gram Panchayat at Garhi Malehra on August 15, 1970
The Victory of the Congress candidates deepened the political cleavage and led to complaints and counter-complaints by and against some members of the factions including the appellants
Apprehending danger to his life, the deceased shifted to Chhatarpur in February, 1971
On April 19, 1971, he came to Garhi Malehra from Chhatarpur
The deceased was accosted and offered tobacco and engaged in conversation by Shankar, the absconding accused
While thus engaged, the deceased and his companion, Dindayal (PW 1) and Shankar, Abdulla and Babua proceeded ahead

On reaching the tri-junction of the roads, Shankar took the deceased unawares and placing his hand around the latter's neck fell him on the ground and started snatching the gun which he (the deceased) was carrying
issues: Whether the case against the appellants had been cooked up on account of the political animosity existing between the two factions
Whether there is not an iota of legal evidence to connect the accused with the commission of the offences for which they have been hauled up

Whether it has not at all been established that the appellants were the confederates of Shankar, Abdulla and Babua and that the deceased was murdered in prosecution of the common object of the accused
petitioner_arguments: The case against the appellants had been cooked up on account of the political animosity existing between the two factions
There is not an iota of legal evidence to connect the accused with the commission of the offences for which they have been hauled up
It has not at all been established that the appellants were the confederates of Shankar, Abdulla and Babua and that the deceased was murdered in prosecution of the common object of the accused
respondent_arguments: The evidence is such that no tribunal could legitimately arrive at the inference that the accused is guilty
The conclusions arrived at by the trial Court with regard to the guilt of the appellants are not supported by evidence and have resulted in gross failure of justice
court_reasoning: Although in an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, this court does not normally re-appraise the evidence and interfere with the finding of the lower Court as to the guilt or innocence of the accused
Where the evidence is such that no tribunal could legitimately arrive at the inference that the accused is guilty, it would not hesitate to set aside the conviction
holding: The convictions of the appellants are quashed
